paragraphs: Unless the context indicates otherwise, any references herein to the "Company", "we", "us" and "our" refer to (i) SBC Medical Group, Inc. (formerly known as SBC Medical Group Holdings Incorporated), a Delaware corporation ("Legacy SBC"), and its consolidated subsidiaries and variable interest entity ("VIE"), prior to the consummation of the Business Combination and to (ii) SBC Medical Group Holdings Incorporated, the Combined Entity and its consolidated subsidiaries and VIE following the Business Combination, and reference herein to "Pono" refers to Pono Capital Two, Inc., the predecessor company prior to the consummation of the Business Combination.

We were originally incorporated in Delaware on March 11, 2022 under the name "Pono Capital Two, Inc.," referred to herein as "Pono," as a special purpose acquisition company formed for the purpose of effecting a merger, capital stock exchange, asset acquisition, stock purchase, reorganization or similar business combination with one or more businesses.

On August 9, 2022, Pono consummated its IPO of 11,500,000 units (the "Units" and, with respect to the Class A common stock included in the Units being offered, the "Public Shares" and with respect to the warrants included in the Units, the "Public Warrants") (the "Pono IPO").

Simultaneously with the consummation of the closing of the Pono IPO, Pono consummated the private placement of an aggregate of 634,375 units (the "Placement Units") at a price of $10.00 per Placement Unit in a private placement to the Sponsor (the "Private Placement").
On September 26, 2022, the Class A common stock and Public Warrant included in the Units began separate trading on The Nasdaq Global Market under the symbols "PTWO" and "PTWOW," respectively.

On January 31, 2023, Pono entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger (as subsequently amended from time to time, the "Merger Agreement") with Pono Two Merger Sub, Inc., a Delaware corporation ("Merger Sub") and then a wholly-owned subsidiary of Pono, SBC Medical Group, Inc., then named SBC Medical Group Holdings Incorporated, a Delaware corporation ("Legacy SBC"), Mehana Capital LLC, a Delaware limited liability company ("Sponsor" or "Purchaser Representative") in its capacity as the representative of the stockholders of Pono, and Yoshiyuki Aikawa in his personal capacity and his capacity as the representative of the stockholders of Legacy SBC ("Seller Representative").

On September 17, 2024, the closing (the "Closing") of the merger (the "Merger") and other transactions contemplated thereby (collectively, the "Business Combination") took place and the Merger was consummated with Merger Sub merging with and into Legacy SBC with Legacy SBC surviving the Merger as a wholly-owned subsidiary of Pono, and Pono then changed its name to SBC Medical Group Holdings Incorporated and on September 17, 2024, Legacy SBC changed its name to SBC Medical Group, Inc.

Effective September 17, 2024, Pono's units ceased trading, and effective September 18, 2024, SBC's common stock began trading on the Nasdaq Global Market under the symbol "SBC" and the public warrants began trading on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbol "SBCWW."
As a result of the Closing of the Merger and the Business Combination, the business of SBC Medical Group, Inc. ("Legacy SBC"), became the business of the Company.

The Company is a management company with offices in Irvine, California and Tokyo, Japan, and, through our subsidiaries, we provide management services to aesthetic clinics in Japan that are owned and operated by medical corporations and other franchisees we support. We also own and operate clinics in Vietnam and Singapore, and we are pursuing U.S. market initiatives primarily through strategic investments and alliances. The history of Legacy SBC began with the establishment of L'Ange Cosmetique Co., Ltd. in 2003 and SBC Japan (formerly Aikawa Medical) in 2017 for the purpose of providing management services to medical corporations and the medical clinics of the medical corporations. The history of the medical corporations and the medical clinics began in 2000 with the opening of Shonan Beauty Clinic in Fujisawa City, Japan, where Dr. Aikawa opened in private practice. Subsequently, Dr. Aikawa opened clinics in Yokohama in 2001 and Shinjuku in 2003, incorporated as Medical Corporation Shobikai in 2004, acquired a medical corporation named Medical Corporation Kowakai in 2009 and Medical Corporation Nasukai in 2009.

The Company and its subsidiaries are primarily focused on providing comprehensive management services to franchisee clinics. These services include advertising and marketing across various platforms (such as social media networks), staff management (such as recruitment and training), booking and reservation services for franchisee clinic customers. We also support franchisee clinics through assistance with employee housing rentals and facility rentals, leasehold improvements and design of clinics, medical equipment and medical consumables procurement (resale), the provision of cosmetic products to clinics for resale to clinic customers, licensure of the use of patent-pending and non-patented medical technologies, trademark and brand use, IT software solutions (including but not limited to remote medical consultations), management of the customer rewards program (customer loyalty point program), and payment tools.

In 2017, we began providing our management services to our franchisee treatment centers. Unless otherwise indicated, the operational metrics in this section are as of December 31, 2025. As of December 31, 2025, the Company and its subsidiaries provided management services to a total of 237 franchisee treatment centers located in Japan, including 5 independently operated clinics in Japan under separate franchise arrangements. In addition, we operate 21 treatment centers in Singapore through Aesthetic Healthcare Holdings ("AHH") and its subsidiaries. The Company also (i) owned and operated 1 treatment center under its "SBC" brand name in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, as well as (ii) previously provided management services to 1 treatment center under its "SBC" brand name in Irvine, California in the United States (the "CA Clinic"), which was owned and operated by the related party, until it was permanently closed at the end of May 2025, and we no longer provide management services to any clinic in the United States. However, in the United States, we have pursued market entry through a strategic minority equity investment in OT Midco, through which we hold an indirect minority interest in the OrangeTwist business ("OT"), and we may explore potential commercial arrangements with OT on a non-binding basis. OT operates 24 treatment centers across the United States, rather than through directly owned and operated clinics or management service arrangements. Our franchisee treatment centers in Japan, together with our treatment centers in Singapore and Vietnam, provide an array of surgical and non-surgical medical services that vary based upon location, including cosmetic surgery, dermatology, and dentistry. These medical services include but are not limited to breast augmentation, liposuction, rejuvenation treatments (including treatment of wrinkles, acne, scars, cellulite, excess fat, discoloration, and signs of aging), laser skin toning and spot removal, eyes double fold surgery, rhinoplasty, treatment of osmidrosis and hyperhidrosis, hair transplants, gynecological formation treatments, laser hair removal, face line surgeries, cosmetic dental procedures, tattoo removal, lasik eye surgery, lateral canthoplasty, brow lift procedures, androgenetic alopecia treatment, and cheek sagging prevention methods.
To further our growth and global expansion, we have recently completed or announced several strategic transactions and initiatives:

• In November 2024, we acquired a 100% equity interest in Aesthetic Healthcare Holdings ("AHH") and its subsidiaries, which are incorporated in Singapore and principally engaged in medical aesthetics business, for cash consideration of SGD$7.8 million (equivalent to approximately US$5.8 million). As a result of this acquisition, we operate clinics in Singapore owned and operated through AHH and its subsidiaries.

headings: Risks Relating to Our Business and Industry
We are a holding company and depend upon our operating subsidiaries for our cash flows.
We may need additional capital, and we cannot be sure that additional financing will be available.
We may not grow our franchise system or we may lose business by failing to compete effectively or by failing to manage the reputation of our brand.
The financial performance of our franchisees and other alliance partners can negatively impact our business.
We could face liability from or as a result of our franchisees and other alliance partners.
We have limited control with respect to the operations of our medical corporation customers, which could have a negative impact on our business.
The challenging economic environment may affect our franchisees, with adverse consequences to us.
Our reputation and the trading price of our common stock may be negatively affected by adverse publicity or detrimental conduct against us.
We are a relatively young company with a short operating history, and we may not be able to sustain our rapid growth, effectively manage it or implement our business strategies.
Our franchisee and other alliance clinics may not be successful in competing in the cosmetic clinic industry.

The Company may face competition from senior management who cease working for it, and the Non-Competition Agreements (as defined below) may be unenforceable and expire two years following the Closing.
Any significant change in the customer reward program at our franchisee and other alliance clinics could have a negative impact on our business.
Any significant cybersecurity incident or disruption to our operating systems could subject us to significant reputational, financial, legal and operational consequences.
Uncertainties with respect to the development, and use of artificial intelligence in our business and products may result in harm to our business and reputation.
We may be compelled to undertake product recalls or take other actions, which could adversely affect our brand image and results of operations.
We may become subject to product liability claims or warranty claims, which could harm our financial condition and liquidity if we are not able to successfully defend or insure against such claims.

We have limited experience in providing management services to franchisee clinics located outside of Japan and we are subject to a variety of costs and risks due to our continued international expansion.
Our operations may be interrupted by utility shortages or stoppages, fire, natural disaster or other calamities at or near our facilities.
Our business and prospects depend significantly on our ability to build our Shonan Beauty Clinic brand.
Any decline in the business of our business partners or the deterioration of our relationship with them could have a material adverse effect on our operating results.
Safety issues or public perceptions of safety issues concerning cosmetic services could have a material adverse impact on our business.
Failure to safeguard personal information could subject us to penalties, damage our reputation and brand, and harm our business and results of operations.
paragraphs: An investment in our securities carries a significant degree of risk. You should carefully consider the following risks, as well as the other information contained in this Annual Report, including our historical financial statements and related notes included elsewhere in this Annual Report, before you decide to purchase our securities. Any one of these risks and uncertainties has the potential to cause material adverse effects on our business, prospects, financial condition and operating results which could cause actual results to differ materially from any forward-looking statements expressed by us and a significant decrease in the value of our common shares and warrants. Refer to "Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements."

We may not be successful in preventing the material adverse effects that any of the following risks and uncertainties may cause. These potential risks and uncertainties may not be a complete list of the risks and uncertainties facing us. There may be additional risks and uncertainties that we are presently unaware of, or presently consider immaterial, that may become material in the future and have a material adverse effect on us. You could lose all or a significant portion of your investment due to any of these risks and uncertainties.

We are a holding company. Almost all of our operations are conducted, and almost all of our assets are owned, by our operating subsidiaries. Consequently, our cash flows and our ability to meet our obligations depend upon the cash flows of our operating subsidiaries and the payment of funds by these operating subsidiaries to us in the form of dividends, distributions or otherwise. The ability of our operating subsidiaries to make any payments to us depends on their earnings, the terms of their indebtedness, including the terms of any credit facilities and legal restrictions. Any failure to receive dividends or distributions from our operating subsidiaries when needed could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations or financial condition.

Although we currently anticipate that our available funds and cash flow from operations will be sufficient to meet our cash needs for the foreseeable future, we may require additional financing to meet our long-term liquidity needs as we continue to execute our business strategy. Our ability to obtain financing will depend, among other things, on our development efforts, business plans, operating performance and condition of the capital markets at the time we seek financing. We cannot assure you that additional financing will be available to us on favorable terms when required, or at all. If we raise additional funds through the issuance of equity, equity-linked or debt securities, those securities may have rights, preferences, or privileges senior to the rights of our common stock, and the existing stockholders may experience dilution.

Our success and growth prospects depend on the strength and desirability of our brand. We believe that potential franchisees choose clinics based primarily on the value and quality of the brand and services, the extent to which affiliation with that franchisor may increase the franchisee's revenue, and the franchise management service fees charged. Demographic, economic or other changes in markets may adversely affect the desirability of our brand and, correspondingly, the number of clinics franchised.

The terms of new franchise management service agreements may not be as favorable as our current franchise management service agreements. For example, we may be required to reduce or change fee structures due to regulatory changes, make greater use of financial incentives such as loans and guaranties to induce the MCs to open new clinics and/or reduce the level of property improvements required before operating under our brand names. This could potentially impact our margins negatively. In addition, unfavorable borrowing conditions may discourage potential franchisees from expanding or constructing new clinics, thereby limiting a source of growth of the franchise management service fees received by us.

paragraphs: On December 13, 2025, the Company announced the final results of the tender offer (the "Tender Offer") conducted by SBC Medical Group Co., Ltd. ("SBC Japan") for shares of the common stock of Waqoo, Inc. ("Waqoo"), a Japanese corporation listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Growth Market.
Below is a summary of the Tender Offer and the results:
• Tender Offeror: SBC Medical Group Co., Ltd. • Target: Waqoo, Inc. (TSE Growth: 4937) • Securities Sought: Common stock of Waqoo
• Offer Period: November 14, 2025 through December 12, 2025 • Offer Price: ¥1,900 per share
• Maximum Number of Shares to Be Purchased: 575,000 shares • Minimum Number of Shares to Be Purchased: None
• Total number of shares tendered: 637,817 shares • Total number of shares purchased: 575,052 shares
• Settlement Agent: SBI SECURITIES Co., Ltd.

As the total number of tendered shares exceeded the maximum planned purchase volume of 575,000 shares, the Tender Offeror purchased shares on a pro rata basis in accordance with Japanese tender offer regulations. As a result, a total of 575,052 shares were purchased, and the remaining shares in excess of such allocation were not purchased, on December 19, 2025.

In addition, the Company's CEO, also the largest shareholder of Waqoo, transferred all of his remaining shares to SBC Japan through an off-market transaction outside of the Tender Offer, also effective as of December 19, 2025. As a result of these transactions, along with the previously held equity interest in Waqoo, SBC Japan's ownership ratio of the voting rights of Waqoo exceeded 50% as of the settlement date.

paragraphs: 除非文意另有明確指示，本文中任何提及「本公司」、「我們」、「我們」及「我們的」均指 (i) SBC Medical Group, Inc.（原名為 SBC Medical Group Holdings Incorporated），一家特拉華州公司（「Legacy SBC」），及其合併子公司與可變利益實體（「VIE」），在完成業務合併前，以及 (ii) SBC Medical Group Holdings Incorporated，合併後的實體及其合併子公司與 VIE，並本文中提及「Pono」指 Pono Capital Two, Inc.，即在完成業務合併前的前身公司。
我們最初於 2022 年 3 月 11 日在特拉華州註冊成立，公司名稱為「Pono Capital Two, Inc.」， herein 簡稱為「Pono」，為一特殊目的收購公司，成立目的為進行合併、資本股票交換、資產收購、股票購買、重組或類似業務合併，與一個或多個企業。
2022 年 8 月 9 日，Pono 完成其首次公開發行（IPO）共 11,500,000 單位（「單位」，與單位中包含的 A 級普通股為「公開股份」，與單位中包含的認購權為「公開認購權」）（「Pono IPO」）。
同時於 Pono IPO 交易完成時，Pono 進行私人 placements，共發行 634,375 單位（「Placement 單位」）每單位價格為 10.00 美元（「Private Placement」）。
2022 年 9 月 26 日，單位中包含的 A 級普通股與認購權開始在 Nasdaq Global Market 分別交易，代碼為「PTWO」與「PTWOW」。

2023 年 1 月 31 日，Pono 與 Pono Two Merger Sub, Inc.，一家特拉華州公司（「Merger Sub」）及當時為 Pono 全資子公司、SBC Medical Group, Inc.（原名為 SBC Medical Group Holdings Incorporated，一家特拉華州公司（「Legacy SBC」）），Mehana Capital LLC，一家特拉華州有限責任公司（「Sponsor」或「股東代表」）在作為 Pono 股東代表的資格下，以及 Yoshiyuki Aikawa 在其個人資格下及作為 Legacy SBC 股東代表的資格下，簽訂合併與重組協議（後經不時修正，稱為「合併協議」）。

2024 年 9 月 17 日，合併（「合併」）及其他相關交易（ collectively，「業務合併」）完成，合併 Sub 與 Legacy SBC 合併，Legacy SBC 繼續存續為 Pono 的全資子公司，並於 2024 年 9 月 17 日，Pono 更名為 SBC Medical Group Holdings Incorporated，同時 Legacy SBC 更名為 SBC Medical Group, Inc.
自 2024 年 9 月 17 日起，Pono 的單位停止交易，自 2024 年 9 月 18 日起，SBC 的普通股開始在 Nasdaq Global Market 交易，代碼為「SBC」，而公開認購權開始在 Nasdaq Capital Market 交易，代碼為「SBCWW」。
因合併交易及業務合併完成，SBC Medical Group, Inc.（"Legacy SBC"）的業務成為本公司之業務。

本公司為一家管理公司，辦公室位於美國加州爾灣及日本東京，透過我們的子公司，我們為日本由醫療公司及其他我們支持之特許經營者所擁有及經營的美容診所提供管理服務。我們亦擁有並營運越南及新加坡的診所，並透過戰略投資及合作關係積極進軍美國市場。Legacy SBC 的歷史可追溯至 2003 年成立 L'Ange Cosmetique Co., Ltd.，以及 2017 年成立 SBC Japan（原為 Aikawa Medical），目的是為醫療公司及其醫療診所提供管理服務。醫療公司及醫療診所的歷史則可追溯至 2000 年，當時日本 Fujisawa 城市的 Shonan Beauty Clinic 開幕，Dr. Aikawa 開設私人診所。隨後，Dr. Aikawa 於 2001 年在 Yokohama 開設診所，2003 年在 Shinjuku 開設診所，2004 年設立 Medical Corporation Shobikai，2009 年收購 Medical Corporation Kowakai，以及 2009 年收購 Medical Corporation Nasukai。

本公司及其子公司主要專注於為特許經營診所提供全面管理服務。這些服務包括跨多種平台（如社交媒體網路）的廣告與行銷、員工管理（如招募與培訓）、為特許經營診所客戶提供預約與預訂服務。我們亦透過協助員工租賃住宅及場地、租賃改善與診所設計、醫療設備與醫療消耗品採購（再銷售）、向診所提供美容產品供再銷售給診所客戶、專利待審及非專利醫療技術的使用許可、商標與品牌使用、資訊科技軟體解決方案（包括但不限於遠距醫療諮詢）、客戶獎勵計畫管理（客戶忠誠點計畫），以及付款工具等，支持特許經營診所。

2017 年，我們開始為我們的特許經營治療中心提供管理服務。除非另有說明，本節的運營指標均為 2025 年 12 月 31 日的數據。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司及其子公司為位於日本總計 237 家特許經營治療中心提供管理服務，包括日本 5 家獨立運營的診所，透過不同的特許經營安排。此外，我們透過 Aesthetic Healthcare Holdings（"AHH"）及其子公司在新加坡營運 21 家治療中心。本公司亦（i）在越南胡志明市擁有並營運 1 家以 "SBC" 品牌為名的治療中心，以及（ii）先前為位於美國加州爾灣的 1 家以 "SBC" 品牌為名的治療中心（"CA Clinic"）提供管理服務，該治療中心由關聯方擁有及營運，直至 2025 年 5 月底永久關閉，我們不再為美國任何診所提供管理服務。然而，在美國，我們透過戰略少數股權投資 OT Midco，間接持有 OrangeTwist 商業（"OT"）的少數權益，並可能在非約束性基礎上探索與 OT 的潛在商業合作關係。OT 透過其自身運營 24 家治療中心，而非透過直接擁有及營運的診所或管理服務安排。我們在日本的特許經營治療中心，加上在新加坡及越南的治療中心，提供一系列根據所在地而有所不同之手術及非手術醫療服務，包括美容手術、皮膚科及牙科等。這些醫療服務包括但不限於乳房增大的手術、吸脂手術、煥膚治療（包括治療皺紋、青春痘、疤痕、脂肪堆積、色素沉澱及老化跡象）、雷射皮膚均勻化及斑點去除、重眼皮手術、鼻整形手術、治療嗅覺過敏及多汗症、植髮、婦科整形治療、雷射脫毛、臉部線條手術、美容牙科程序、紋身去除、雷射角膜手術、眼角整形手術、眉毛提升程序、雄激素性脫髮治療及顴骨下垂預防方法。
為進一步推動成長與全球擴張，我們近期已完成或宣佈了數項戰略交易與計畫：
• 2024 年 11 月，我們以現金 7.8 百萬新加坡幣（約當 5.8 百萬美元）取得 Aesthetic Healthcare Holdings（"AHH"）及其子公司 100% 的股權，該公司註冊於新加坡，主要從事醫療美容業務。因本次收購，我們透過 AHH 及其子公司擁有並營運位於新加坡的診所。

paragraphs: 於 2025 年 12 月 13 日，本公司宣佈 SBC Medical Group Co., Ltd.（"SBC Japan"）進行的標單購併（"標單購併"）最終結果，該標單購併係針對 Waqoo, Inc.（"Waqoo"）普通股，Waqoo 為於東京證券交易所成長市場上市之日本公司。
以下為標單購併及結果之摘要：
• 標單購併人：SBC Medical Group Co., Ltd. • 目標公司：Waqoo, Inc.（TSE Growth: 4937） • 所求股份：Waqoo 普通股
• 標單購併期間：2025 年 11 月 14 日至 2025 年 12 月 12 日 • 標單購併價格：每股 1,900 日圓
• 最多購入股份數量：575,000 股 • 最少購入股份數量：無
• 標單購併股份總數：637,817 股 • 購入股份總數：575,052 股
• 設定代理人：SBI SECURITIES Co., Ltd.
因標單購併股份總數超過預計購入之 575,000 股，標單購併人依照日本標單購併規則，按比例購入股份。因此，總計購入 575,052 股，剩餘未經分配之股份於 2025 年 12 月 19 日未購入。
此外，本公司董事長，同時也是 Waqoo 最大股東，已透過非公開交易方式，將其持有的所有股份轉讓給 SBC Japan，該交易亦自 2025 年 12 月 19 日起生效。因應這些交易，加上 SBC Japan 之前持有的 Waqoo 股權，SBC Japan 在 Waqoo 票據權的持股比例於結算日已超過 50%。

headings: 與我們業務及產業相關之風險
本公司為一控股公司，我們的現金流取決於我們營運子公司。
我們可能需要額外資金，且我們無法確定是否能取得額外融資。
我們可能無法擴大特許經營體系，或因未能有效競爭或未能管理品牌聲譽而失去業務。
我們特許經營者及其他合作夥伴之財務表現可能對我們業務產生負面影響。
我們可能因特許經營者及其他合作夥伴而面臨責任或損失。
我們對醫療公司客戶之營運控制有限，這可能對我們業務產生負面影響。
困難的經濟環境可能影響我們特許經營者，進而對我們造成不利後果。
本公司對特許經營商之集中度相當高。
本公司聲譽及普通股之交易價格可能因對本公司之不利宣傳或損害行為而受到負面影響。
本公司為相對年輕之公司，營運歷史較短，可能無法持續我們快速之成長，有效管理該成長或執行我們之商業策略。
本公司之特許經營商及其他合作診所可能無法在美容診所產業中成功競爭。
本公司可能面臨來自前高階管理階層之競爭，且非競爭協議（如下所定義）可能無法執行，且在交易完成後兩年內屆期。
本公司特許經營商及其他合作診所之客戶獎勵計畫如有重大變更，可能對本公司業務造成負面影響。
若發生重大網路安全事件或對本公司營運系統之幹擾，可能使本公司面臨重大聲譽、財務、法律及營運後果。
有關本公司業務及產品中人工智慧之發展與應用之不確定性，可能對本公司業務及聲譽造成損害。
本公司可能被迫進行產品回收或採取其他行動，這可能會對本公司品牌聲譽及營運結果產生不利影響。
本公司可能成為產品責任索償或保証索償的對象，若本公司無法成功抗辯或投保以對抗這些索償，可能會對本公司財務狀況及流動性造成損害。
本公司在為日本境外的加盟診所提供管理服務方面經驗有限，且因持續進行國際擴張，而面臨多種成本與風險。
本公司營運可能因設施所在地或附近發生電力短缺或停擺、火災、自然災害或其他災難而中斷。
本公司業務與前景在很大程度上取決於本公司建立小金澤美容診所品牌的能力。
本公司業務夥伴業務表現下滑或與本公司關係惡化，可能會對本公司營運結果產生重大不利影響。
有關美容服務安全問題或公眾對安全問題的觀感，可能會對本公司業務產生重大不利影響。
未能妥善保護個人資料，可能會使本公司遭受處罰、損害聲譽與品牌，並對本公司業務及營運結果造成損害。
paragraphs: 投資本公司的證券具有相當程度的風險。您應仔細考慮下列風險，以及本年度報告中包含的其他資訊，包括我們的歷史財務資料及相關附註，再決定是否購買本公司證券。任何一種風險與不確定性都可能對本公司業務、前景、財務狀況與營運成果造成重大不利影響，導致實際結果與我們所表達的預測性陳述有重大差異，並可能導致本公司普通股與認股權證價值大幅下降。請參閱「預測性陳述的警示說明」。
我們可能無法成功防止任何下列風險與不確定性所造成的重大不利影響。這些潛在風險與不確定性可能並非我們所面臨的全部風險與不確定性。未來可能還有我們目前未察覺，或目前認為不重要，但之後可能變得重要的風險與不確定性，並對我們造成重大不利影響。您可能因任何一種風險與不確定性而損失全部或相當大一部分的投資。
本公司為控股公司。幾乎所有營運活動均由我們的營運子公司進行，幾乎所有資產也由營運子公司擁有。因此，我們的現金流與履行義務的能力，取決於營運子公司現金流，以及這些營運子公司向我們支付現金的股息、分紅或其他方式。營運子公司能否支付現金給我們，取決於其營收、負債條款，包括信貸融資條款與法律限制。若無法在需要時收到營運子公司支付的股息或分紅，可能對本公司業務、營運成果或財務狀況造成重大不利影響。

雖然我們目前預期現有資金與營運現金流足以應付可預見的未來的現金需求，但我們可能需要額外融資以應付長期流動性需求，尤其是在持續執行業務策略的過程中。我們能否取得融資，取決於多種因素，包括我們的開發努力、業務計畫、營運表現與當時資本市場的狀況。我們無法保證在需要時，能以有利條件取得額外融資，或甚至無法取得融資。若我們透過發行股權、股權連結或債務證券來籌資，這些證券可能享有優先權、特別權或優先權利，現有股東可能因此遭遇稀釋。
我們的成功與成長前景取決於品牌強度與吸引力。我們認為潛在特許經營商選擇診所主要基於品牌與服務的價值與品質、與該特許經營商合作是否能提高特許經營商的營收，以及收取的特許經營管理服務費用。市場的族羣、經濟或其他變動可能對我們品牌的吸引力造成不利影響，進而影響診所特許經營的數量。
新特許經營管理服務契約的條款可能不如我們現行的特許經營管理服務契約有利。例如，我們可能因法規變動而必須降低或改變費用結構，或更廣泛使用財務誘因，如貸款與擔保，以誘導MCs開設新診所，或減少在以我們品牌名稱營運前所需的財產改善程度。這可能會對我們的毛利率造成負面影響。此外，不利的貸款條件可能使潛在特許經營商放棄擴張或興建新診所，從而限制我們收到特許經營管理服務費用的成長來源。
